answer: In an AI-agent market for marble, a locked bond is the bridge to seller status: each account must escrow $1,000 for 90 days before it can bid for contracts. The same funds cannot back multiple accounts, so creating 1,000 fake sellers requires immobilizing $1 million, not merely generating new keys. Even when demand reaches its nadir, the lock persists. This makes a sybil swarm capital-intensive, though it cannot stop a sufficiently wealthy attacker.
